import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 484

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/484](https://www.erdosproblems.com/484)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [ESS89] Erdős, P., Sárközy, A., and Sós, V. T., *On a conjecture of Roth and some related
  problems. I*. (1989), 47-59.
-/

namespace Erdos484

open scoped Classical in
/--
Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, whenever $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is
$k$-coloured (and $N$ is large enough depending on $k$) then there are at least $cN$ many
integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which are representable as a monochromatic sum (that is, $a+b$
where $a,b\in \{1,\ldots,N\}$ are in the same colour class and $a\neq b$).

A conjecture of Roth. Solved by Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós [ESS89], who in fact prove that
there are at least $\frac{N}{2}-O(N^{1-1/2^{k+1}})$ many even numbers which are of this form.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos484.lean"]
theorem erdos_484 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → ∀ f : ℕ → Fin k,
      c * N ≤ (((Finset.Icc 1 N).filter fun n =>
        ∃ a ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, ∃ b ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
          a ≠ b ∧ f a = f b ∧ a + b = n).card : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos484

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over colourings ℕ → Fin k rather than functions defined only on {1,…,N}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Only values on Finset.Icc 1 N occur in the predicate. Every global colouring restricts to this interval, and, because k > 0, every interval colouring extends globally by assigning colour 0 outside it. These operations preserve the counted set. The full quantified statements were proved equivalent in /workspace/review/colour_equiv.lean.

reformulations.difference: The theorem uses a real, non-strict lower bound cN for N ≥ N₀. Er61 and Er80 use strictly more than cN above a strict threshold; the linked formal proof instead bounds the cardinality below by ⌊cN⌋₊.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These forms are equivalent because c is existential and positive and the threshold may increase. Strict thresholds can be shifted by one. A non-strict linear bound becomes strict after replacing c by c/2 and taking N > 0. A floor bound implies the real bound with constant c/2 once N > 2/c, since ⌊cN⌋ > cN − 1; conversely, a real lower bound implies its floor version. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/floor_equiv.lean.

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the source problem: c is independent of k, N₀ is uniform over colourings, and the filter counts distinct integers in [1,N] admitting a sum of two distinct, same-coloured positive summands. Checked Fin, interval, filter, cardinality, and coercion semantics. Scratch tests cover empty and small intervals, the one-colour identity card = N − 2, parity colouring, and exhaustive two-colourings through N = 10. The source records PROVED (LEAN), consistent with both metadata attributes. The exact linked proof compiled under the installed Lean/Mathlib. Combining it with the floor equivalence derives the repository's exact statement in /workspace/review/proof_bridge.lean, independently of the repository's sorry; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The reviewed file was not modified.
